# Transformation for dates (class Date)

Transformation for dates (class Date)

## Usage

``` r
transform_date()

date_trans()
```

## Examples

``` r
years <- seq(as.Date("1910/1/1"), as.Date("1999/1/1"), "years")
t <- transform_date()
t$transform(years)
#>  [1] -21915 -21550 -21185 -20819 -20454 -20089 -19724 -19358 -18993
#> [10] -18628 -18263 -17897 -17532 -17167 -16802 -16436 -16071 -15706
#> [19] -15341 -14975 -14610 -14245 -13880 -13514 -13149 -12784 -12419
#> [28] -12053 -11688 -11323 -10958 -10592 -10227  -9862  -9497  -9131
#> [37]  -8766  -8401  -8036  -7670  -7305  -6940  -6575  -6209  -5844
#> [46]  -5479  -5114  -4748  -4383  -4018  -3653  -3287  -2922  -2557
#> [55]  -2192  -1826  -1461  -1096   -731   -365      0    365    730
#> [64]   1096   1461   1826   2191   2557   2922   3287   3652   4018
#> [73]   4383   4748   5113   5479   5844   6209   6574   6940   7305
#> [82]   7670   8035   8401   8766   9131   9496   9862  10227  10592
t$inverse(t$transform(years))
#>  [1] "1910-01-01" "1911-01-01" "1912-01-01" "1913-01-01" "1914-01-01"
#>  [6] "1915-01-01" "1916-01-01" "1917-01-01" "1918-01-01" "1919-01-01"

#> [26] "1935-01-01" "1936-01-01" "1937-01-01" "1938-01-01" "1939-01-01"
#> [31] "1940-01-01" "1941-01-01" "1942-01-01" "1943-01-01" "1944-01-01"
```
